title: 3.3.11 Lab: countWords(text)
description: Write countWords(text): split a sentence at its spaces and return how many words there are. Practice with split and length, not graded: the checks call your function.

steps.title: Write countWords
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration called countWords that takes one parameter, text. The words in text are separated by single spaces, and there is always at least one word.

steps.title: Split it into words
steps.instructions: Inside the function, cut text at every space with text.split(" ") (3.3.10). That gives you an array with one item per word.

steps.title: Return the count
steps.instructions: Return how many items that array has, using .length (3.3.2).

steps.title: Check it
steps.instructions: Call countWords with a sentence and console.log the result.

requirements.title: countWords is defined with one parameter
requirements.description: Code defines a function named countWords with exactly one parameter. Help: 3.3.10 (Splitting Text into Lines (.split))
requirements.hint: Write function countWords(text) { ... } with exactly that name and one name between the parentheses.

requirements.title: countWords splits the text
requirements.description: countWords calls .split( in its body. Help: 3.3.10 (Splitting Text into Lines (.split))
requirements.hint: Use .split(" ") on the text parameter to get an array of words.

requirements.title: countWords hands back a value with return
requirements.description: countWords contains a return statement. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: The answer must leave the function with return, not console.log.

requirements.title: countWords counts the words
requirements.description: countWords(text) gives back how many words the text has, when the words are separated by single spaces. Help: 3.3.10 (Splitting Text into Lines (.split))
requirements.hint: Split at a space, .split(" "), and return the length of the array. Splitting at "" (nothing between the quotes) cuts the text into letters, not words, and splitting at "\n" only cuts at line breaks.
